doc.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025

title: Moving to L.A. with no contacts and then leaving for New York
summary: He arrived with 50 dollars, met Terry Trotter, studied with Victor Aller, did studio work within a year, and left in 1984 as synthesizers took over, joining Mulligan in New York.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: It must have been a big decision to move – you know across the country to New York after you’ve established yourself in Los Angeles. What was the impetus for that?

I’m crazy. I’m fearless. You know I moved to Los Angeles with 50 dollars in the bank. Seriously. And I had – I don’t think I had one contact. I knew Terry Trotter, the marvelous pianist, through his records, and I called Terry before I got to Los Angeles and told him I was going to be moving up and I’d love to meet him. And we became friends. We used to play four-hand classical music at his Steinway. And Terry recommended me for some gigs almost immediately. And then I fell in with other musicians like Mike Lang and Charlie Shoemake, Bobby Shew. And I got my name around town fairly quickly. I also started studying with an excellent classical teacher there, Victor Aller. And I told him that I wanted to break into the studios and what did he think. What did I need. And he helped me immensely with tone production, with sight reading, and within a year I was doing studio work. So it was a quick learning experience. And then I spent 15 years as I said, and I left in 1984. One of the reasons I left is that studio keyboardists were becoming less pianists and more synthesizer programmers. And I’d been very successful doing this and I didn’t want to keep doing it for the rest of my life, again for some of the same reasons that I moved to Los Angeles, I wanted to leave L.A. so that I’d have an

opportunity to play with people in New York which I did. I got the gig with Gerry Mulligan immediately and got a chance to play with Al Cohn and Bob Brookmeyer and the Vanguard band and the list goes on.
